speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: They signal to consumers that a product has a special quality, reputation or other characteristics by virtue of its geographical location and origin.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The GI Registry is run by the Intellectual Property Office of Singapore (IPOS).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: It commenced operations on 1 April 2019, after the EU Parliament ratified the EUSFTA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: In this time, IPOS has become more familiar with the operations of a GI Registry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: GI labels cannot be used on products which do not come from the place indicated by the GI evidently if this misleads the public as to the true geographical origin of those products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This is applicable for all GIs, whether they are registered or not.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: In addition, for wines and spirits, such GI labels cannot be used on products which do not come from the place indicated by the GI, even if consumers are not misled as to the true geographical origin of the goods in question.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Registered GIs which are not for wines and spirits would enjoy the same level of protection for GIs which are for wines and spirits mentioned earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Producers and traders in respect of registered GIs also have access to border enforcement measures such as being able to request that our Customs authorities detain suspected infringing goods which are to be imported or exported from Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: I will now take Members through the main features of the Bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The first set of amendments in the Bill clarifies how variants of a GI are to be treated during the application process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: A variant of a GI can be a translation, or a transliteration, or any other variation of the indication constituting the GI.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Say, for example, that oranges grown on Pulau Ubin are known to bear a unique and highly-prized sweet and sour quality attributable to the natural environment of Pulau Ubin, and such oranges are known by the Chinese characters 乌敏橙 – in Chinese – oranges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Such oranges might be referred to in slightly different ways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: So, let me give Members the different ways in which it could be referred to.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: For example, they may be referred or identified in Hanyu Pinyin as "Wu Min Cheng", which is a transliteration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Or they may also be known as "Ubin Orange", which is a translation of the words in Chinese.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: They could also be called "Pulau Ubin Orange", which is neither a translation nor a transliteration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: All of these can be variants of a GI and they can be registered.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The GI Registry has received a number of applications where, in a single application, multiple variants of the nature that I have described, constituting the same GI were included.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This, no doubt, saved application fees for the applicant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: These applications were accepted as-is and most of them have, in fact, been registered.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: It is proposed in this Act that we amend and clearly state how such applications and registrations with multiple variants should be treated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: So, for example, in a situation where multiple variants of a GI have been registered, a party may want to apply to cancel the registration because he finds one of the variants objectionable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: If he is successful, it is not clear whether the entire GI registration should be cancelled, or whether there should only be a partial cancellation, that is, only of the particular variant that he finds objectionable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Clauses 3, 4, 6 and 8 of the Bill, therefore, amend the GI Act to clarify the following.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: First, an application for registration can contain more than one variant constituting the same GI.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Second, after an application for registration is accepted and published for public inspection, third parties who oppose the application can choose to oppose the registration of one or more of the variants in the application, instead of all of the variants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Third, where there is a refusal of registration of a variant, the other variants in the application for registration can nevertheless be registered if they satisfy the requirements of the Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The second set of amendments makes changes to the process for the entry of a Qualification of Rights in the Register.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: A request for a Qualification of Rights, or more commonly known as a QoR, to be entered in the Register, is a request usually taken up by a third party, in order to clarify the scope of protection that the GI Act confers on a registered GI, in relation to whether a name or a term contained in the GI or a term which may be a translation of the GI is available for use by the third party.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: To take up the example that I outlined earlier, let us say the producers of Wu Min Cheng oranges applied for the registration of that GI for oranges, including all the variants which I have mentioned previously.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Now, a Mr Wu Min Cheng, an individual who is a seller of oranges, he could request a QoR to be entered in the GI Register to state that he can rely on the exception in section 13 of the Act for the use of his personal name.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: If he is successful, he can continue to use the personal name, his personal name in relation to the oranges that he sells, even if these oranges are not of the Wu Min Cheng variety or originating from Pulau Ubin.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: However, the producers of Wu Min Cheng oranges can prevent Mr Wu from using the other registered variants, such as "Ubin Oranges", for example, for selling his oranges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Such a QoR also does not affect the ability of the producers of Wu Min Cheng oranges from bringing an action against other producers for labelling their products as Wu Min Cheng oranges, in other words, producers other than Mr Wu.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This is different from opposing the application for registration or applying to cancel the registration of a GI, whether in respect of one or all the variants, because the reason for opposition or cancellation is that the GI or variant should not be protected as a registered GI at all.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The end result of a successful opposition or cancellation of the registration of a particular variant is that the variant is not allowed to be registered or is removed from the GI Register.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: If the opposition or cancellation was against the entire set of variants, the end result is that the entire set of variants is not registered or is removed from the GI Register.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: After the GI Registry commenced its operations, we found that certain types of QoR requests could achieve the same result as a successful opposition or cancellation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: To illustrate the point, for instance, a QoR request could possibly be so broad as to result in a situation where the interested parties of a GI are effectively left with no rights in respect of a registered GI that they can enforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The QoR process was intended to enable an applicant to clarify the scope of protection conferred by the registration, and not to negate the GI registration altogether by wholly removing the rights conferred by registration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: For example, a qualification of all the rights conferred in respect of a registered GI may not be requested on the basis that the GI or variant is identical with the common name of the goods concerned in Singapore, as such a QoR would result in there being no rights conferred on a registered GI that can be enforced in respect of the registered GI or variant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This, therefore, makes it very clear that the QoR regime and the opposition or cancellation regime remains separate and distinct.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: They are meant as two different sets of parameters and protocols meant to apply to obtain two different sets of remedies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Applicants seeking to negate the rights conferred under the Act in respect of a registered GI or variant will not be able to use a QoR request as a substitute for opposition or cancellation proceedings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Currently, QoR requests can be filed any time after the GI application is published.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The requests are dealt with by the Registrar of GIs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: However, in the course of operating the GI Registry, IPOS has found the need to treat pre-registration and post-registration QoR requests differently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Pre-registration QoR requests relate to GI applications which are still pending before the Registrar.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: It would be more efficient for the Registrar to handle all pre-registration processes together, whether oppositions or QoR requests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: In this way, the application for registration can be handled as expediently as possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This also ensures that the applicant as well as third parties can have clarity about the protected rights as soon as possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: On the other hand, once a GI has been registered – and this is the post-registration – there is no specified timeframe for post-registration processes to be initiated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Further, GI disputes are often global in nature, with disputes around the world based on similar facts and issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Given the desirability of taking into account the arguments and outcomes of disputes in other countries as well when determining a post-registration QoR request, we, therefore, feel that the Registrar might not be the best forum for the determination of such disputes, especially when there is no longer an efficiency gain in doing so, in the same way as I have explained the pre-registration process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Nonetheless, we recognise that there may be disputes as to the scope of the protection conferred upon a registered GI post-registration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The scope of such applications, and the grounds on which such applications can be granted, are set out in the new section 48(a), inserted by clause 7 of the Bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Having these issues dealt with by the Courts would also give the opportunity for Singapore decisions to be cited by Courts in other jurisdictions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The changes I mentioned previously providing that a QoR request cannot be used to negate the registration of a GI or a variant, will also apply in the context of this new procedure for application for a Limitation of Scope of rights.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This was in line with our international obligations under the EUSFTA.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Under the Schedule of the GI Act 2014, the categories of goods that a GI may be registered under relate to foodstuff or agricultural products.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: For countries where there are a lot of exports of such items that qualify for GI, GIs help build up the reputation and quality associated with the produce in a different country.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Although Singapore is not an agricultural exporting country, GIs are still relevant to us.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Singaporeans enjoy and consume food from all over the world.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Therefore, GIs add assurance relating to the unique flavour and authenticity of the product.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This Bill makes the GI framework clearer through two key avenues: (a) the qualification and limitation of rights; and (b) variants of GIs.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: At this juncture, I declare for the Hansard record that I am a lawyer and some of my work relates to intellectual property (IP) rights.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: After registration, clause 7 inserts a new section to provide for a very similar process post-registration, albeit the term "limitation of scope" instead of "qualification" is used.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Would the Minister elaborate on why the process, which in substance appears the same, has been bifurcated into pre- and post-registration?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The process is important as it sets out more clearly what is protected and what is not protected.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This clarity facilitates better usage and protection of GIs by providing a better indicator for those who may be concerned over a potential infringement.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Further, clause 5(d) and the new section 48(4) in clause 7 delineate when a qualification or limitation is appropriate and when a notice of opposition is appropriate.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This provides needed guidance and ensures that the more appropriate process is used in any given circumstance.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The other main group of amendments relate to variants in a GI.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Variants play an important role in the IP right of GIs.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: When a product's reputation and market expand across the globe, it and its GI would probably have to be translated or transliterated in order to be represented in a different language.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: By protecting other forms, such as translations and transliterations, we protect the essence of the GI such that merchants are unable to circumvent the protection of GIs by simply changing the form in which it is presented.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This affords a more complete protection and assists in establishing a global market.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It not only helps preserve authenticity and quality of products related to the GI but also makes them more accessible to people who speak a different language.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In relation to this, the illustration in the Explanatory Statement for clause 2 refers to "Lion City Apples" as a variant for "Apples of Singapore." I must say a much less exciting example than "Pulau Ubin Oranges".

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I do like the ring of "Pulau Ubin Oranges".

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Would the Minister explain under what circumstances would a nickname for a place be recognised as a variant under the GI?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: For official nicknames used widely and even at national celebrations, such as a National Day Parade, it is clear that it is quite well-known and accepted.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: However, there are times when the nickname may not be as widely known or accepted.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Under those circumstances, would such "unofficial" nicknames be accepted?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Clause 3 allows an application for a variant to be separate from the main application or together with it.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This flexibility is welcomed and allows for the accommodation of market forces, for instance, where the demand for goods change such that the GI should be translated into a different language in order to have the full benefit of the IP right in question.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In short, this Bill makes the regime clearer.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In particular, it prescribes how the Act should be interpreted in respect of variants of a GI as well as clarifying the legal procedure by which an appellant can seek to qualify or limit the scope of the rights conferred by the registration of the GI.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Through bringing about these certifications, the Bill is a significant step in the right direction.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I have a few questions and suggestions for the Minister in respect of this Bill.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Before I raise these, I would like to declare my interest as the Chief Executive Officer of a research consultancy that undertakes work in the agrifood and processed food and beverage space among other product categories.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: GIs are terms which are used to inform consumers that a product, mostly food and drinks, comes from a particular place.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Perhaps the most famous example of a GI is champagne.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Other examples are Tennessee whiskey, Pinggu peaches, Darjeeling tea and Parmesan cheese.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Essentially, GIs must identify goods where the qualities, characteristics or reputation of the product should be essentially due to the place of origin.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: GIs help consumers gain assurance that the product they are buying embody the geographically grounded characteristics reflected in the product name.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: My first question would be, as a Singaporean consumer purchasing a product where a GI has been registered in Singapore, how can they obtain some degree of assurance that the product they are purchasing is a genuine GI product, as it were, rather than a product from a different region that has usurped the name protected under the registered GI?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: No doubt, once the GIs are registered, producers and traders of the GI products will be able to request customs authorities to "detain suspected infringing goods which are imported into or exported from Singapore", as IPOS declared in the media report.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But the ability of producers and traders of GI products to enforce their rights may be uneven on the ground.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Can IPOS consider working with GI rights holders, industry associations and other stakeholders to create an easy-to-use directory entirely funded by GI rights holders which will list legitimate products bearing the GI by brand, product type and retailer?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Industry stakeholders will be strongly incentivised to fund such a directory.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Next, GIs represent an opportunity for local farming and food processing entrepreneurs to brand Singaporean products for enhanced competitiveness in export markets while also potentially contributing to the tourist experience for inbound tourists into Singapore who may seek good quality local food.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In fact, it is not uncommon for tourist authorities to promote local foodstuffs and where they can be obtained.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) Asia Office said, as quoted in a media report by Food Navigator Asia, and I quote, "As the industry moves towards globalisation and bringing local products to the world, local or ethnic products are increasingly becoming a target for GIs as these are often the most popularly searched by tourists.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is becoming increasingly important to differentiate your products from the pack.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The time for uniformity in food and beverage (F&B) is gone and GIs are going to be a big contributor to this." In this context, I have two other questions.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The GI system that is being set up – and you have seen it operate in the last year or so – is obviously designed to achieve the purposes for which Mr Leon Perera has outlined: to give a platform to recognise local producers, to give a basis on which to differentiate and to distinguish food products in particular, and to operate a system on which you can say that something is domain to the location and that, in itself, is a distinguishing feature.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And so, the purpose of this regime is really to set up an environment that promotes all of these and allows protection to be given to producers so that they can then leverage on the GI, or rather, the name of a product linked to the geographical location, in the context of Mr Leon Perera's point in Singapore as well.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Christopher de Souza asked why the process is being bifurcated into a pre- and a post-registration.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But let me just reiterate the concept and also the paradigm by which this is to be operating.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In this context, the Registrar that handles the pre-registration QoR request together with the GI application will enable an efficient and expedient processing of the matters.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The new Limitation of Scope process is dealt with by the Courts and not by the Registrar.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And as Mr Christopher de Souza knows, it is common for the GIs around the world to be based on similar facts and issues.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There may be competing interests; there may be disputes on the factual circumstances and matrix which give rise to the GI and they often involve similar, if not identical parties, as Mr Christopher de Souza will know.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Therefore, there may be decisions by foreign courts which would provide guidance and, indeed, it would also guide the nature of the decision in Singapore and vice versa.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And in this context, it will be an opportunity for Singapore jurisprudence to be used in other countries as well.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Given the above, the Courts, we feel, will be better placed to adjudicate on these matters.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Christopher de Souza also asked about "Lion City Apples" and the use of the nickname and the circumstances under which the nickname for a place would be recognised as a variant of a GI, and under what circumstances that nickname could then be accepted.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This would be done as part of the application for registration process before the Registrar of GIs.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As for Mr Leon Perera's queries, the Singapore consumer obviously would also rely on the similar processes to ensure that there is no improper usurpation of the name.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And that each time a GI is registered, there will be a thorough, exhaustive review of the circumstances giving rise to the claim for that particular GI.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The suggestion that there may be a set-up that is used, funded by GI rights holders so that there can be a proper categorisation by brands and so on, is something we can consider.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I think that is a useful suggestion insofar as it takes the debate further on how branding can be better organised, how there can be searches and ultimately leading to better enforcement and policing of those rights.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The second point Mr Leon Perera raised which I agreed with earlier is that this entire platform that the GI Act has created is indeed useful for Singapore producers because Singapore producers can then leverage our own geographical location and, indeed, there are several special places within Singapore whose names are very well associated with certain types of foods.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And, to that extent, that can be used.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Will the Government consider working with these producers?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: What we do see is that the reforms that we make, not just in this Bill itself but generally in the context of the IP space, we see this as an opportunity for local producers, local companies to take advantage of the laws that we set up.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As I have mentioned on more than one occasion, we ensure that the laws that we set up have, in other words, to be very much pro-business and centred on the needs of the user.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, if we are able to have a platform where producers, manufacturers can take advantage of and protect the GIs, then certainly, we will encourage them to do so and to see what further assistance can be offered so that there will be even more Singapore producers beyond the examples that Mr Christopher de Souza and myself have outlined, which are illustrative only, I might add.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And the system that we have set up, put in place about a year ago, and now enhanced with these amendments, is designed to further all of these.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The changes that are being introduced reflect our continual effort to look at, update and enhance the IP regime and provide a fair and transparent GI regime.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This, we believe, will further enhance our reputation as the IP hub of the region.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 5.05 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 4.41 pm until 5.05 pm.
